Westside today · how Westside talks×

Westside speaks through YNG, Wesness and FRONT ROW.

The everyday voice is warm and inclusive; the events are editorial. Nothing yet links the two, or takes people from a post into a store.

What Westside says now

  • New Indian talent. YNG creators, 30 New Faces, FRONT ROW.
  • Culture beyond clothes. I-pop, dance-offs, fitness runs.
  • Women together. Wesness runs in four cities, 3,600+ at the biggest.
  • Own labels first. Bombay Paisley, E.T.A, Utsa, Vark, W Edit.

Where we take it

  • Shoppers rarely hear about the 400–500 new designs a week. Tell them, store by store.
  • Turn festive edits into one story from Navratri to the wedding season, in store and on Instagram.
  • Give every new store the same local launch, with creators and looks styled from its rails.
  • End every post and every event in a store, and count the visit.

Styled by Westside

Starts with YNG’s creators and the new designs that land every week.

The Westside Coffee Cart

Goes where Westside already gathers people, from Wesness finish lines to launch weekends.

Window Stories

Casts FRONT ROW’s New Faces as the couples and families in the windows.

The plan×

The test: one city, twelve weeks, three ideas, 15 mn impressions.

Westside’s biggest published content figure in the last year is 6 mn YNG views. The test targets 15 mn impressions in twelve weeks, and at least 20% more reach than Westside’s best comparable campaign of the last year. Built on what Westside already runs: YNG, Wesness and FRONT ROW.

1

Styled by Westside

Every week, stylists and creators build complete Westside looks in store, film them and post them on Westside’s, creators’ and paid city pages.

Where it ends

Each look has a code. Show it at the store and the team brings the outfit in your size.

Idea 1 of 3×
Styled by Westside

Make styling the reason people follow Westside.

Almost everything Westside sells is its own label, and its designers create 400–500 new designs a week. Most people never see how those pieces go together. Every week our stylists and creators build complete looks from one Westside store, film them on the floor and post them on Instagram and YouTube Shorts.

Each look has a code. Show it in store and the team brings the whole outfit in your size, or holds it if a size is out. The code is not a discount: it tells the team which look you want, and tells us which post brought you in.

One piece, three ways

A stylist takes one Westside piece from office to dinner to a family function.

Style me for…

A creator brings a real occasion. Our stylist dresses them from one store in thirty minutes.

Head to toe, one budget

Clothes, shoes and Studiowest make-up, every piece from the store, with the total on screen.

Stylist vs creator

Same brief, two looks, the audience picks. The winner gets the front rail for a week, with the store manager’s sign-off.

Designs: Bloomberg interview with Shailina Parti, 20 Jul 2026, as reported by Retail Insight Network. Own labels: BW Businessworld, 2026. Featured looks use lines with stock depth, signed off by Westside’s buying team.08 / 22

The Westside Coffee Cart

Coffee, and the look that goes with it.

A Westside-designed coffee cart that parks outside Westside stores, in malls, at colleges and in office parks. The menu is named after Westside’s own labels, and every cup sleeve carries a look code to show at the nearest store.

On the menu

  • Bombay Paisley Filter
  • Nuon Cold Brew
  • Gia Hazelnut Latte
  • Wardrobe Flat White
  • Utsa Masala Chai
  • Vark Rose Cardamom

How people see it

Creators and clip, city and food pages film the cart, the cups and the queue. We pay for those posts, which is how three carts reach 5.4 mn impressions.

Idea 3 of 3×
Window Stories

Rahul and Anjali are getting ready for a date.

Two mannequins dressed for a moment everyone knows, with every piece on them for sale inside. It is a window people stop to photograph and share.

Next month the story changes: a first day at a new job, a cousin’s mehendi, Sunday lunch at Nani’s, a college reunion.

Each story is two complete outfits, each look priced on a card in the window, with a code to ask for it in store. Anjali’s dressing table is set with Studiowest, priced on the same card.

Illustration is a concept drawing. Character names are working titles until the story list is approved.12 / 22

From post to bill×

How every idea reaches the billing counter.

1

Made in store

A stylist or creator builds the look from one store’s rails; the cart and the windows carry looks from the same rails.

2

Posted the same week

Westside’s pages, the creator’s page and paid clip and city pages carry the same look.

3

Tagged with a code

Every post, cup sleeve and window card shows a short look code and the store’s name.

4

Shown at the store

The shopper shows the code. The team brings the look in their size.

5

Logged at billing

The code goes on the bill. Westside’s analytics team matches it to WestStyleClub bills; we see store totals only.

The look code links each post, cup and window to a store and a bill. That is how we count sales from content. The code is never a discount.

Store teams need one short briefing a week: this week’s looks, where they hang and how to log the code.

Against Westside’s best published figure

YNG, views6 mn
This test, impressions15 mn

Views count plays; impressions count every showing. In week one we swap in Westside’s best comparable campaign of the last twelve months and commit to beat its reach by at least 20%. If organic reach is behind plan by week six, we move budget into paid Reels.

Inputs: clip and city pages at 35,000 views a post, from a Qoruz report via Social Samosa, 2025 (₹1 lakh buys 10–20 meme-page posts and 500,000+ views). Reels ads at ₹45–140 per 1,000 impressions in India (Upgrowth, 2026), planned at ₹120. Westside and creator averages are planning figures, replaced with real averages in week two. Low = 60% of organic, high = 150%; paid is fixed.15 / 22
Measurement×

Measured at the billing counter.

Impressions show the work was seen; footfall and bills show it worked. We report both weekly, store by store.

Draft threshold

Test-city stores beat matched stores on entries by 5% or more over the twelve live weeks. We set the final number from your data before launch.

What we countHowRead against
Footfall per storePeople counters at the entranceTest-city stores against matched stores that did not get the programme
Codes usedLook codes from posts, cups and windows, logged at billingPer store, per idea, per week
Member billsCodes matched to WestStyleClub bills by Westside’s analytics teamMembers who used a code against members who did not
Impressions and viewsPlatform reports from every page and creatorAgainst the plan, line by line, every week

A launch store has no history, so it is read against the opening weeks of recent comparable openings. One store can show a lift of about 10%; a city’s stores pooled can show smaller lifts. We see store totals only, never personal data.

The test×

Start with one city. If the numbers don’t move, you lose nothing.

Twelve weeks live, all three ideas, read on footfall per store. Pick what the test is built around.

Option A · recommended

A store launch

Westside’s next opening and the stores in its city: looks styled from its rails before it opens, the Coffee Cart outside on opening weekend, Window Stories across the city.

Read against the opening weeks of recent comparable openings, and against matched stores.

Option B

The wedding season

One city through the wedding dates: styled looks for every function, the cart at the city’s busiest Westside, wedding Window Stories in every store.

Read against each store’s previous twelve weeks and matched stores in other cities.

If it works

Our fee, agreed now, is paid only if footfall beats the threshold.

If it doesn’t

No fee, and Mask360 carries production and media for the test, within a cap agreed before launch.

What we need from Westside

A test city and matched stores, a look-code field at billing, stock depth on featured looks, VM time, help with mall consent, counter and bill data under a data agreement, and sign-off on each week’s posts within 48 hours.
